what: A WebGL ring-line field is laid behind the plate. 28 rings (27 on phone) circle a horn and ball shape, flowing latitude 0→1 over 6 seconds as they appear and fade, rippling like contour lines with fbm noise. Six scenes (top-down contours · close-up horn · slanted ball · tilted horn · side profile · front view) each hold for 4s and switch over 2s with expo inOut as the view rotates. Moving the cursor fast speeds the flow from .22→.62, twists the area around the cursor (radius .16) into a swirl, and the viewpoint follows by .015. A grain roughness (.13) overlay covers the whole screen.

options.rings: Number of rings, default 28 (27 on phone)
options.life: Seconds for one ring to pass latitude 0→1, default 6
options.scene: Give 0~5 to stay on that scene (no spinning)
options.cycle: If off, stays on the first scene
options.parallax: Amount the viewpoint follows the cursor, default .015
options.swirl: Strength of the swirl around the cursor, default .065 (off on phones) — 0 turns it off
options.grain: Grain roughness strength, default .13 — 0 turns it off

from.where: index.html #md-hero(hero.js) — original HeroWebGL(three r184): ringCount 28/27 · ringLifetime 6 · cycle hold 4 / transition 2 · flowVelocity .22–.62(phone .31–.70) · distort swirl radius .16 strength .065 · grain .13 · parallax .015, scene values were measured from the original settings and carried over

note: We did not use the original shader or code and wrote our own shader (ring ribbon, noise, one finishing pass). The original uses three EffectComposer passes (warp·distort·grain), while this part merges them into one render target + one shader. First-time visitors start at the first scene, returning visitors at a random scene (localStorage)
